Where to Stay in Songkhla?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Songkhla & Hat Yai hotels across every budget — from an Old Town boutique on Nang Ngam Road and a Samila beachfront resort down to a hostel in central Hat Yai from ฿315/night. Covering the main areas: Songkhla Old Town and Samila Beach, central Hat Yai, and Ko Yo on the lake. From roughly ฿315–1,800/night.
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Songkhla matter so much?
introHtml: In Songkhla, where you stay really shapes the trip, because the main draws sit in different zones. Songkhla Old Town and Samila Beach (the Bo Yang district) is the slow-travel zone — Nang Ngam, Nakhon Nok and Nakhon Nai roads, Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafés, street art, and Samila Beach with its mermaid statue — ideal for wandering, photos and the seaside. Central Hat Yai sits about 30 km from Songkhla town, but it's the hub for shopping, food, Kim Yong Market, Central Festival mall and Hat Yai airport — best for shoppers, foodies and people on a layover. And Ko Yo, an island in Songkhla Lake, suits those who want a quiet lakeside stay, sea-bass restaurants and views of the Tinsulanonda Bridge. Many people book in Hat Yai expecting an easy day out to the Old Town and Samila Beach, then burn the day driving 30 km back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Songkhla and Hat Yai hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Songkhla has no metro; you get around by car, motorbike and songthaew, and the province is spread out enough that your choice of area sets up the whole trip. Stays in the Songkhla Old Town and Samila Beach area (Bo Yang) are walkable to Nang Ngam Road and the seafront, but they're about 30 km from Hat Yai. Central Hat Yai stays are within walking distance of Kim Yong Market, Central Festival mall and the Lee Garden area, and closest to Hat Yai airport. Ko Yo needs a private or rental car, as it's an island in the lake reached across the Tinsulanonda Bridge. The areas in this guide: Songkhla Old Town & Samila Beach — wander the old town, the seaside, cafés · Hat Yai — shopping, food, the airport, layovers · Ko Yo — a lakeside stay and sea bass.

entries.name: Casa de Si Boutique House
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · 19 reviews · top-scoring Old Town boutique

tags: 🏛️ Vintage boutique in the Old Town

entries.addr: 83 Nakhon Nok Rd, Bo Yang, Mueang Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: Casa de Si Boutique House takes the top score in this guide at 9.3 — a vintage boutique house in the heart of Songkhla's Old Town on Nakhon Nok Road, an easy walk to Nang Ngam Road, the cafés and the street art. Real guest reviews praise the characterful vintage styling, the clean rooms, the attentive owner, and the Superior Seaview rooms that look out over Songkhla Lake. The trade-off: it's a small boutique with limited rooms, no pool, and a modest review count (19 reviews). Best for couples and Old Town lovers who value design and a walkable location over a full set of facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an upper-floor Superior Seaview room overlooking the lake — it's the signature view here. Rooms are few and sell out fast on long weekends, so book ahead. Wander Nang Ngam Road in the morning or evening to dodge the heat; the cafés and street art are close by.

entries.name: Shi-ro-i Poshtel
tags: 🛏️ Curtained dorm pods + roomy private rooms
🚶 Central Hat Yai, walk to food
entries.storyHtml: Shi-ro-i Poshtel is a Japanese-style poshtel in central Hat Yai that scores 9.2 from 336 reviews — the highest and most-reviewed in this guide's budget tier. Its selling point is Japanese-grade cleanliness, dorm pods with their own curtains and partitions, and roomy ~36 sqm Deluxe private rooms for those who want privacy. Real guest reviews praise how clean it is, the friendly staff, and the central location within walking distance of food. The catch: it's a hostel-style stay — no pool, no full breakfast, and the dorms use shared bathrooms. Best for solo travellers, pairs and budget travellers who prize cleanliness and location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: On a tight budget, take a dorm bed from ฿360 — the pods have curtains for reasonable privacy. Want a private room? The ฿700 Deluxe Room is roomy for the price. The central location makes it easy to walk out for Hat Yai street food.

entries.storyHtml: Laguna Grand Hotel & Spa is the most fully-equipped 4-star in this guide, scoring 9.1 from 508 reviews, with a big swimming pool and a spa. It sits in Phawong, midway between Songkhla town and Hat Yai, so you can drive either way. Real guest reviews praise the spacious, clean, fresh rooms (from 35 sqm), the large pool, the spa, and the standard of service. The trade-off: Phawong isn't in the Old Town or Hat Yai centre, so you'll need a car to head out, and dining around the hotel is thin. Best for families and anyone wanting a big-pool hotel with roomy rooms to base both-town sightseeing from.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family? Book a Grand Deluxe (42 sqm) or above for comfort. Make the most of the pool and spa — they're the highlight. The mid-point location is about a 15–20 minute drive to both the Old Town and Hat Yai, so have a car ready.

entries.storyHtml: Centara Hotel Hat Yai is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide — 3,374 reviews — connected directly to the Central mall in the heart of Hat Yai, scoring 8.7. It's a frequent pick for shoppers and people on a layover, because you walk straight from your room into the mall, with Hat Yai's food and market streets all around. Real guest reviews praise the most convenient location in town, the Centara-standard rooms, and the pool and fitness centre. The catch: it's one of the city's older hotels, so some reviews note the rooms and facilities are starting to age, and the rates run higher than many in-town options. Best for shoppers, foodies and layover travellers who want the most convenient mall-linked location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The draw is the direct mall link — ask for a higher-floor city-view room for better value. It's the best base for Hat Yai souvenir shopping or a layover. Rates spike on long weekends when Malaysian and Singaporean shoppers arrive, so book ahead.

entries.storyHtml: Sri Koh You Resort is a small resort on Ko Yo, the island in Songkhla Lake, for travellers who want a quiet lakeside stay at a budget price, scoring 8.4 from 12 reviews. Ko Yo is a lake island known for its sea-bass restaurants and views of the Tinsulanonda Bridge. Real guest reviews praise the peaceful setting, the clean, good-value rooms, and the parking at your door. The catch: it's a small resort with few facilities and no pool, a small review count, and you really need a car since it's on the island, far from both the town and Hat Yai. Best for self-drivers who want a lakeside stay, Ko Yo sea bass, and the Tinsulanonda Bridge.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Songkhla hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in, in Songkhla?
faq.a: It depends on your trip's goal. Songkhla Old Town & Samila Beach (Bo Yang) suits those who want to wander Nang Ngam Road, photograph the Sino-Portuguese shophouses and visit Samila Beach (Casa de Si, Baan Nai Nakhon, BP Samila). Central Hat Yai suits shoppers, foodies and layover travellers, with malls, Kim Yong Market, Central Festival and the airport close by (Centara, Crystal, Buri Sriphu, Shi-ro-i, BP Grand Tower, WE Hostel). Ko Yo suits a quiet lakeside stay and sea bass (Sri Koh You). The Old Town and Hat Yai are about 30 km apart.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Songkhla hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels and budget stays start around ฿315–750 a night (WE Hostel, The Bedrooms, Shi-ro-i Poshtel, Sri Koh You); mid-range to 4-star hotels and boutiques run about ฿850–1,800 (BP Grand Tower, Crystal, Baan Nai Nakhon, Laguna Grand, BP Samila, Casa de Si, Buri Sriphu, Centara). All are approximate starting rates for standard rooms; on long weekends and festivals, Hat Yai prices run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ For Songkhla Old Town and Samila Beach, where should I stay?
faq.a: If the Old Town and Samila Beach are your main focus, stay in the Bo Yang area so you can explore on foot — Casa de Si Boutique House ฿1,400, the top-scoring boutique on Nakhon Nok Road; Baan Nai Nakhon ฿1,200, an old house right on Nang Ngam Road; and BP Samila Beach ฿1,400, on Samila Beach so you wake to the sea. This whole area is about 30 km from Hat Yai, so allow driving time if you'll go there too.

faq.q: ❓ For shopping and eating in Hat Yai, where should I stay?
faq.a: For shopping and food, central Hat Yai is most convenient. Centara Hotel Hat Yai ฿1,800 connects to the Central mall and is the most-reviewed; Crystal Hotel Hat Yai ฿900 sits next to Central Festival, a great-value 4-star; Buri Sriphu ฿1,500 is central with food within walking distance. On a budget, Shi-ro-i Poshtel ฿700 or WE Hostel ฿315 are near the food zone and Lee Garden.

faq.q: ❓ Can I get around Songkhla without a car?
faq.a: Songkhla has no metro, so without a car, staying in central Hat Yai or the Songkhla Old Town is most convenient — Hat Yai has plenty of songthaews and dense streets, with food within walking distance (Shi-ro-i, Crystal, Centara, WE Hostel); in the Old Town you can walk Nang Ngam Road and Samila Beach. For Ko Yo (Sri Koh You) and Phawong (Laguna Grand), have a car or Grab ready. The Old Town and Hat Yai are about 30 km apart, with vans and songthaews running between them.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Songkhla hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so it's worth comparing all three before every booking — each review page in this guide has a price-comparison link, which can save several hundred baht a night, especially for Hat Yai hotels over long weekends and festivals when foreign shoppers arrive.
